_comment: AUTH MANIFEST - how each agent CLI authenticates. Data, not code.
TWO LEVELS, and the split matters:
providers[]  a backend and its SHARED attributes. A region or an API key
belongs to the provider, not to each CLI that uses it, so
configuring a provider once serves every CLI that uses it.
methods[]    one (cli, provider) pairing plus only what is specific to it -
typically the model id and, for codex, a gateway URL.
WHY: v1 put every attribute on the method, so two methods sharing one
provider both wrote a bare `model` key and each silently overwrote the
other's. Shared things now live in one place and method-specific things are
namespaced by method id. It is also the grouping the UI renders: one
collapsible section per provider.
PORTABILITY: nothing here names a user, a drive letter, a region, a model or a
URL. Those live in ~/.agentmux/auth.json (0600) under providers{} and methods{},
written by taskmgmt/setup_auth.py.
SECRETS NEVER LIVE HERE and never travel through the browser. A provider declares
the NAMES of the environment variables it needs; values are written to
~/.agentmux/env (0600) by a non-echoing terminal prompt, and agentmux SOURCES
that file into each pane rather than interpolating it into a command line - so a
key never appears in `ps`, in tmux's pane_start_command, or in shell history.
settings[].validate names a validator in taskmgmt/setup_auth.py PROMPTS.
checks / setup use the same vocabulary as resources.json; setup commands are
SHOWN to the operator and never run by the server.

providers.label: ChatGPT account
providers.summary: A ChatGPT plan, via browser sign-in. The CLI owns the token; agentmux holds nothing.
notes: Subject to a weekly plan quota. When it is exhausted codex stops mid-task and says so - it does not silently fall back to another method.

providers.label: Anthropic account
providers.summary: Interactive sign-in to a Claude plan.
notes: Windows keeps this login in the DPAPI credential store, which Linux cannot read, so WSL needs its own login. No symlink can share it.

providers.label: Anthropic API
providers.summary: Direct Anthropic API billing instead of a plan.

providers.label: Google Vertex AI
providers.summary: GCP-hosted models. Credentials come from gcloud ADC, so there is no key for agentmux to hold.
notes: Nothing is stored in ~/.agentmux/env for this provider - the credential is the gcloud ADC file.

providers.label: xAI account
providers.summary: Device-code sign-in to a Grok account. No API key needed.
notes: Usage is billed per request even with a browser login.

providers.label: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
providers.summary: vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM, Azure OpenAI - anything speaking the OpenAI Responses API.
notes: The endpoint must implement the Responses API. A chat-completions-only endpoint will not work with this codex version.
